newsitem.title: USA: Jury deliberations begin in Oklahoma bomb trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberations begin in Oklahoma bomb trial.

text.p: The jury in the trial of Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh began deliberating on his guilt or innocence on Friday after five weeks of testimony.
"You will retire and begin your deliberations in this case," federal Judge Richard Matsch said after giving the jury final instructions on the law and how they must treat evidence in the case.

McVeigh is accused of blowing up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people in the worst attack on civilians in U.S. history. The decorated Gulf War veteran, 29, has pleaded not guilty to murder and conspiracy charges. He could face the death penalty if convicted.
Jury deliberations began at 9.33 A.M. (11.33 A.M. EDT).
"You are not to be swayed by sympathy, you are to be guided solely by the evidence in this case," Matsch instructed the jurors during his hour-long instructions.

"If you have a reasonable doubt, you should not hesitate to return a verdict of not guilty," he said. "The question can never be, will the government win or lose this case. The government always wins when justice is done regardless of whether the verdict is guilty or not guilty."
